intended_object: The ring isomorphism K₀(K) ≅ ℤ for a field K, sending the class of a finite-dimensional vector space to its dimension, where K₀ carries the ring structure coming from the tensor product (Weibel, K-book, II §2). Inferred from the docstring and name.
explanation:
The definition faithfully gives the standard isomorphism K₀(K) ≅ ℤ for a field K, sending the class of a vector space to its dimension.

How it is built: it takes the library's additive equivalence `finrankEquiv : K0 K ≃+ ℤ` (built from the integer-dimension map) and upgrades it to a ring isomorphism. To do so it proves that the map is multiplicative. That step uses the fact that the inverse sends z to z • [K], and [K] is the unit of the K₀ ring (`intCast_eq_zsmul`). So the forward map is exactly the dimension map, extended to formal differences, which is the standard isomorphism.

Generality: the field hypothesis is the natural one for this statement as a ring isomorphism. The ring structure on K₀ comes from the tensor product, so it needs a commutative ring. For a division ring the library only provides the additive equivalence (`finrankEquiv`). The library also proves more general versions separately: `localRingEquivInt` for local rings and `pidRingEquivInt` for PIDs. The field case is the classical statement in its own right, so it is not "too narrow".

Mathlib counterpart: none. Mathlib has no algebraic K₀ of rings, so there is nothing to cite.
